purpose: Public clean-room research atlas of systems that reconstruct, generate, simulate, plan, or assist 3D worlds. HAYUYA copies architectural lessons, not proprietary models, layouts, assets, prompts, training data, or product internals.

transferableLessons: treat camera, depth and geometry as coupled inference tasks
accept partial geometric priors instead of forcing image-only operation
keep one scene backbone capable of several metric reconstruction tasks
use a second independent geometry hypothesis
judge camera and point consistency rather than trusting a single reconstruction
separate reconstruction, world generation and world simulation capabilities
treat a world model as a modular stack rather than one final mesh button
preserve editable 3D representations downstream of generative stages
camera path can be an explicit conditioning/control signal
RGB and depth should remain aligned during world extension
long-range generation needs a persistent world cache and culling strategy
judge temporal consistency in addition to still-image beauty
world generation and player control must share state
interactive latency is a separate engineering target from offline quality
world creation should accept heterogeneous modalities
worlds should support edit, expand and combine operations after generation
coarse layout is a valuable control input, not merely a final output
interactive world simulation should be evaluated over time, not one frame
agent action consequences are part of world understanding
photorealistic visual simulation is not equivalent to editable game-engine geometry
360 proxy generation plus depth can bootstrap scene-scale reconstruction
mesh and splat representations should coexist as different delivery targets
loop closure and global scale consistency need explicit QA
separate scene-layout reasoning from individual asset generation
LLMs are useful for object positions, scales and composition plans
generated assets need production topology/material stages after semantic layout
index the user's existing assets instead of regenerating everything
metadata and creative history form a reusable world-building memory
human editable scene assembly should remain first-class
separate design intent filters from world generation
allow iterative variation rather than one-shot generation
feed accepted design decisions back into later generation stages
procedural rules need live parameters and artist override
large worlds require partition-aware generation
generation graphs should be reusable at asset, biome and world scales

crossSystemArchitectureLessons: Split semantic planning, spatial layout, asset creation, geometry reconstruction, simulation, optimization and runtime compilation into replaceable stages.
Use explicit scene/world graphs as the durable intermediate representation.
Generate multiple hypotheses for expensive or uncertain stages and judge them with independent evidence.
Support text, images, video, maps, depth, meshes, coarse layouts and user corrections as peer evidence sources.
Maintain persistent world state for long-range generation rather than treating every view as an isolated prompt.
Keep editability after generation: objects, regions, materials, routes and gameplay logic should remain addressable.
Use solver agents to test playability; visual beauty alone cannot certify a game level.
Separate offline hero-world quality from real-time/mobile delivery derivatives.
Treat licensing, provenance and provider terms as pipeline metadata rather than after-the-fact paperwork.
